misclassified_entities.original_description: Malicious actor attempting to spam cheap ModExp calls
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: An 'attacker' is a threat model concept describing adversarial intent, not a distinct external entity that sends unique data into the system. The attacker uses the same interface as legitimate callers (EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER). Threat modeling should consider attacker motivations but model them as the same entity type with malicious intent.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Smart contract or EOA invoking the identity precompile
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke the identity precompile at address 0x04. The caller is unauthenticated - the EVM simply routes execution based on target address. The identity precompile correctly treats all input as untrusted and performs no validation, merely copying data to output.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - precompile accessible to any caller

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Any contract or EOA can call the identity precompile with arbitrary data
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Explicitly named 'untrusted' in the specification. This entity represents the security boundary where arbitrary external data enters the identity precompile. The precompile design acknowledges this by performing no validation and returning data unchanged.

trusted_external_entities.entity_name: Contract or EOA Caller / Smart Contract Caller
trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External entity invoking the ModExp precompile via CALL opcode for cryptographic operations
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any contract can call the ModExp precompile at address 0x05. The caller controls the base, exponent, and modulus parameters which determine gas cost. The gas pricing mechanism (minimum 200 gas, complexity-based calculation) exists specifically because callers are untrusted and could attempt DoS via underpriced operations.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - precompile accessible to any caller

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Browser extension (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) injecting EVM provider
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Wallet extensions are installed by the user, implying user intent to trust them. However, they inject executable code and SVG icons into the browser context. The SVG icon security boundary (requiring tag rendering) exists because even user-installed extensions can contain malicious payloads. Extensions are trusted to provide EIP-1193 interfaces but their icon data must be sanitized.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: End user interacting with the decentralized application
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: The user selects which wallet provider to use from the discovered options. User input determines which provider's EIP-1193 interface the DApp will use. Users are trusted to select their intended wallet but may be deceived by malicious extensions masquerading as legitimate wallets.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Application providing ABI specifications for transaction transparency
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: DApps provide ABI specifications that wallets use to decode and display transaction calldata. A malicious DApp could provide intentionally misleading ABIs that make malicious transactions appear benign. The specification explicitly states 'Wallets MAY validate provided specs against trusted databases' because DApp-provided ABIs cannot be trusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - DApp is untrusted web application

trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: This entity explicitly models the threat of a DApp providing fake ABIs to deceive users. The security boundary subgraph shows how misleading ABIs could cause users to approve transactions that perform different actions than displayed. This is a valid external entity representing the adversarial case of EXT-DAPP.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External database of verified contract ABIs
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Databases like 4byte.directory, Sourcify, or Etherscan verified contracts provide reference ABIs for validation. These are semi-trusted because they are external services with their own security models - they could be compromised or provide incorrect data. Wallets should treat them as a helpful validation source but not absolute ground truth.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: Database provider reputation and verification processes

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: End user viewing and approving transactions
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: The user views decoded transaction information and decides whether to approve. Users are trusted to make their own decisions but may be misled by malicious ABIs showing incorrect function interpretations. The user's approval is the final gate before transaction signing.

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Contract calls identity precompile at address 0x04 with arbitrary input data
Untrusted caller provides arbitrary data that passes through identity precompile unchanged
Contract calls ModExp precompile with base, exponent, and modulus for cryptographic computation
Wallet extension content script executes and injects provider into window.evmproviders
Wallet extension provides base64-encoded SVG icon that requires secure rendering
User selects preferred wallet provider from displayed options
DApp includes ABI interface specifications in wallet_sendCalls request for calldata decoding
Potentially malicious dapp provides ABI that may misrepresent transaction functions

coverage_gaps.reason: No explicit incoming edge defined - this entity is queried by the wallet for ABI validation rather than pushing data into the system. Consider as outbound query target.

coverage_analysis.notes: Prague Identity precompile (spec_64eb1c64a143565fcf2c0d119093d4b3482c4832) has minimal security surface - it intentionally performs no validation. EIP-2565 ModExp (spec_658caaaa21ae54f1273b123db778bb2c7f761bcf) has DoS protection via minimum gas floor and complexity-based pricing. EIP-5749 Multi-wallet provider (spec_69172d473f2771c2c2c372707bc2d620c0fef924) has XSS security boundary for SVG icons - DApps MUST use tags. EIP-7896 ABI interfaces (spec_6a7b9a12047975928a78c599d117f0e6f39fc2d1) has significant trust boundary concerns - DApp-provided ABIs can mislead users about transaction intent. EIP-1153 Transient storage (spec_6ba4c793caef698562211d007d4ec6912235b3c9) has no external entities - TSTORE/TLOAD are internal EVM operations with transaction-scoped state.
